paragraphs.title: An Invitation to Praise and Give Thanks to the Lord

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “O come, let us sing unto the LORD.”
easy.q: Whom does the psalmist invite the people to sing unto?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving.”
easy.q: With what should the people come before the Lord’s presence?

easy.explanation: The verse calls him “the rock of our salvation.”
easy.q: How is the Lord described in verse 1?

answers: Singing, making a joyful noise, and giving thanks
medium.explanation: The verses call the people to sing, make a joyful noise, and approach the Lord with thanksgiving.
medium.q: What sequence of actions is emphasized in these verses?

answers: Because he is the rock of their salvation
medium.explanation: Verse 1 identifies the Lord as “the rock of our salvation.”
medium.q: Why should the people praise the Lord according to this passage?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes an enthusiastic expression of praise.
medium.q: What does “make a joyful noise” mean in this context?

answers: Worship can include different joyful expressions of praise
challenge.explanation: The psalm describes both singing and joyful shouting as responses to the Lord.
challenge.q: What does the use of both “sing” and “make a joyful noise” show about worship?

answers: Both describe approaching the Lord with grateful worship
The first describes judgment and the second describes rest
The first describes war and the second describes escape
challenge.explanation: The people come before the Lord with thanksgiving and joyful songs.
challenge.q: How are thanksgiving and joyful praise connected in these verses?

challenge.explanation: The invitation is based on recognizing the Lord as the rock of salvation.
challenge.q: What inner attitude best fits this invitation?

answers: A great God and a great King
easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “For the LORD is a great God, and a great King above all gods.”
easy.q: How is the Lord described in verse 3?

answers: The deep places of the earth
easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, “In his hand are the deep places of the earth.”
easy.q: What is in the Lord’s hand?

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “The sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land.”
easy.q: Who made the sea and formed the dry land?

answers: The deep earth, the mountain heights, the sea, and the dry land
medium.explanation: Verses 4–5 mention the deep places, the strength of the hills, the sea, and the dry land.
medium.q: Which parts of creation are included in the description of the Lord’s rule?

answers: They show that all the earth and sea belong to him and were formed by him
They say that the people chose him as king
medium.explanation: His ownership and creation of the natural world display his greatness.
medium.q: How do verses 4–5 explain the Lord’s greatness?

answers: The height and majesty of the mountains
medium.explanation: The expression refers to the power, height, and grandeur of the hills.
medium.q: What does “the strength of the hills” refer to?

answers: His ownership and authority over all creation
His rule over only one city
challenge.explanation: The passage extends his authority over the earth, mountains, sea, and dry land.
challenge.q: What supports the statement that the Lord is “a great King above all gods”?

answers: The passage lists the areas that display his greatness
The passage changes to the subject of rest
The passage presents an argument between people
challenge.explanation: The descriptions connect different parts of creation to the Lord’s authority.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repeated descriptions of what belongs to the Lord?

answers: Both belong to the Lord and were made by him
The sea belongs to people and the land belongs to the Lord
The sea and land oppose the Lord
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the sea is his and that his hands formed the dry land.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the sea and the dry land in verse 5?

paragraphs.title: Bowing Before the Lord, the Protective Shepherd

easy.explanation: Verse 6 says, “Let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the LORD our maker.”
easy.q: What does the psalm call the people to do before the Lord?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “For he is our God.”
easy.q: Who is the Lord to the people according to verse 7?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “To day if ye will hear his voice.”
easy.q: What are the people called to do if they will hear the Lord’s voice?

answers: Because he is their Maker, God, shepherd, and guide
Because he wants to rest in the wilderness
Because he wants to test the people
medium.explanation: The passage identifies the Lord as their Maker and God and pictures them as his pasture and sheep.
medium.q: Why should the people bow and kneel before the Lord?

answers: Both describe people cared for and guided by the Lord
Both describe the sea and dry land
Both describe the enemies of the people
medium.explanation: Both expressions use the picture of sheep under a shepherd’s care.
medium.q: What is the connection between “the people of his pasture” and “the sheep of his hand”?

answers: The people whom the Lord shepherds and cares for
The people who fight against him
The people who have left him
medium.explanation: The phrase portrays the people as belonging to the Lord’s care.
medium.q: What does the phrase “the people of his pasture” mean?

answers: Worship, acknowledge his care, and listen to his voice
challenge.explanation: The verses connect humble worship and attentive hearing with the Lord’s identity as Maker and shepherd.
challenge.q: What response is appropriate because the Lord is both our Maker and our shepherd?

answers: The need to listen to the Lord in the present
That listening belonged only to a former generation
challenge.explanation: “To day” presents hearing the Lord’s voice as an immediate opportunity and responsibility.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “To day” emphasize?

answers: The people depend on the Lord’s guidance and protection
The people guide and protect the Lord
The people have no connection with the Lord
challenge.explanation: Sheep in a shepherd’s hand represent dependence upon his care and direction.
challenge.q: What does the image of “the sheep of his hand” imply?

paragraphs.title: A Warning Against Hardening the Heart

easy.q: What does the psalm warn the people not to do?

answers: The provocation and the day of temptation in the wilderness
The sea and the dry land
easy.explanation: Verse 8 refers to “the provocation” and “the day of temptation in the wilderness.”
easy.q: What past events are mentioned as warnings?
What did the fathers see even after they tempted and proved the Lord?

answers: They erred in their heart and did not know his ways
medium.explanation: Verse 10 calls them “a people that do err in their heart” who had not known his ways.
medium.q: Why was the Lord grieved with that generation?

answers: They would not enter into his rest
They would see his work for the first time
medium.explanation: Verse 11 says they should not enter into the Lord’s rest.
medium.q: What was the result of the Lord’s oath?

medium.explanation: “Grieved” expresses the Lord’s sorrow and displeasure toward that generation.
medium.q: What does “grieved” mean in the statement “Forty years long was I grieved with this generation”?

answers: Seeing God’s works is not enough if people still test him and refuse his ways
Seeing God’s works removes the need to listen to him
Seeing God’s works proves that people need no guidance
challenge.explanation: The fathers saw the Lord’s work but still tempted him and went astray in their hearts.
challenge.q: What is the connection between seeing the Lord’s work and the warning against hardening the heart?

answers: Hardness of heart can lead to the serious consequence of missing the Lord’s rest
Hardness of heart has no consequence
Hardness of heart immediately leads to praise
challenge.explanation: The passage connects rebellion and unbelief with exclusion from the Lord’s rest.
challenge.q: What does the movement from “Harden not your heart” to the Lord’s oath teach?

answers: The promised land the disobedient generation would not enter
The wilderness where they tested the Lord
The sea formed by the Lord’s hands
challenge.explanation: In this context, the Lord’s rest points to the promised land.
challenge.q: In the context of this passage, what does “my rest” represent?
